newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges France not to patrol no-fly zones.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges France not to patrol no-fly zones.

text.p: Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz on Saturday urged France to stop patrolling two no-fly zones in northern and southern Iraq.
Aziz made his remarks during a meeting with a French parliamentary delegation, headed by MP Roselyne Bachelot.
"The meeting discussed the illegal no-fly (zones) imposed on the north and the south and the necessity that France should review its participation in it," the official Iraqi news agency (INA) said.
France, the U.S. and Britain are imposing two zones, one in the south and another in the north in order to protect the Kurds from any possible attack from Baghdad.

The United States expanded the southern zone to reach the outskirts of Baghdad in September when Iraq sent troops to the north to help one Kurdish faction fighting against a rival one, prompting Washington to launch missile attacks in southern Iraq.
Iraqi Vice-President Taha Yassin Ramadam told the delegation "Iraqi people highly appreciate French world policy."
Ramadan also lauded France for its "efforts in international forums to end the embargo on Iraq", imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
France, China and Russia, all permanent members of the U.N. Security Council, have in the past advocated easing the curbs on Iraqi oil exports.
Chirac said during his visit to Jordan last month that the suffering in Iraq was "unworhty of the modern world."

Iraqi newspapers said on Saturday that French businessmen would arrive in Baghdad this week to hold talks with Iraqi officials trying to conclude trade deals in accordance with an "oil-for-food" agreement signed by Iraq and the U.N.
The deal, stalled over security matters in northern Iraq, allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil in six months to buy food and medicine for the Iraqi people.

Iraq was a main outlet for French goods before the U.N. trade sanctions. France upgraded its representation in Iraq last year, sending a diplomat to run an interests section in Baghdad for the first time since the invasion of Kuwait.
